units.name: Computing Basics & Binary

concepts.intro: A computer is a machine that stores and manipulates data as electrical signals, following a stored program of instructions.
b: The CPU (central processing unit) fetches, decodes, and executes instructions one step at a time
RAM (memory) holds the program and data currently in use; it is fast but erased when power is lost
Storage (SSD/hard drive) holds data permanently, even without power
Input devices (keyboard, mouse, sensors) bring data in; output devices (screen, speaker) send results out
The fetch-decode-execute cycle repeats billions of times per second, measured in Hertz (clock speed)

concepts.intro: Computers represent all data using binary (base-2), a number system with only two digits: 0 and 1, because transistors are easiest to build as simple on/off switches.
b: A single binary digit (0 or 1) is called a bit
8 bits grouped together form a byte, the basic unit of storage (e.g., one character)
Each bit position represents a power of 2: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128...
To convert binary to decimal, add the powers of 2 where there is a 1 (e.g., 1011 = 8+0+2+1 = 11)
To convert decimal to binary, repeatedly divide by 2 and record the remainders
Everything digital — text, images, sound, video — is ultimately stored as sequences of bits

concepts.intro: Hexadecimal (base-16) is a compact way to represent binary values, since each hex digit maps exactly to 4 bits.
b: Hex uses digits 0-9 and letters A-F, where A=10, B=11, C=12, D=13, E=14, F=15
One hex digit represents exactly 4 bits (a 'nibble'), so 2 hex digits represent one byte
Hex is commonly used for colors (#FF0000 = red), memory addresses, and error codes
To convert hex to binary, translate each hex digit into its 4-bit binary equivalent
Decimal (base-10) is what humans normally use; computers use binary internally for hardware simplicity

concepts.intro: Different kinds of data (numbers, text, images, sound) are all encoded into binary using agreed-upon schemes.
b: ASCII assigns each English letter, digit, and symbol a number from 0-127, stored as a byte
Unicode (like UTF-8) extends this to represent characters from virtually every language and emoji
Images are stored as grids of pixels, each pixel's color encoded as binary RGB values
Sound is captured by sampling the wave thousands of times per second and storing each sample as a number
File size depends on how much data is stored: more pixels, higher sample rates, or longer text mean larger files

concepts.intro: A computer's physical hardware works together, with each component playing a specialized role in processing information.
b: CPU: executes instructions; measured in GHz (clock speed) and number of cores
RAM: temporary, volatile working memory; more RAM lets more programs run smoothly at once
Storage (SSD/HDD): permanent, non-volatile; SSDs are faster than traditional spinning hard disks
Motherboard: connects all components together and lets them communicate
GPU: specialized processor originally for graphics, now also used for parallel computations like AI

concepts.intro: The operating system (OS) is software that manages hardware resources and provides a platform for other programs to run.
b: Examples of operating systems: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS
The OS manages memory allocation, scheduling which program uses the CPU, and file storage
System software (like the OS) supports the computer itself; application software (like a browser) helps users do tasks
A file system organizes how data is stored and retrieved from storage devices
Drivers are small programs that let the OS communicate with specific hardware devices

keyFacts: 1 byte = 8 bits; 1 kilobyte (KB) ≈ 1000 bytes; 1 megabyte (MB) ≈ 1,000,000 bytes
Binary 1011 = decimal 11; decimal 25 = binary 11001
ASCII uses 7-8 bits per character; UTF-8 can use 1-4 bytes per character to support all languages
Moore's Law observed that transistor counts (and roughly computing power) doubled about every two years
traps: RAM is temporary/volatile working memory, not permanent storage — data in RAM is lost when power is off
A byte is 8 bits, not 10 bits — binary place values are powers of 2, not powers of 10
The CPU executes instructions; it is the GPU, not the CPU, that is optimized for massively parallel tasks like graphics
Hexadecimal is a human-friendly shorthand for binary, not a separate system computers use internally — hardware still stores everything in binary

units.name: Programming Fundamentals

concepts.intro: A variable is a named storage location that holds a value which can change while a program runs; every value has a data type that determines what operations are valid on it.
b: Common data types: integer (whole numbers), float/double (decimals), string (text), boolean (true/false)
A variable is created (declared) with a name and often an initial value, e.g., age = 16
Variable names should be descriptive and follow naming rules (no spaces, can't start with a digit)
Type matters: adding two integers gives a number, but adding two strings concatenates (joins) them
Some languages require declaring the type explicitly (statically typed); others infer it automatically (dynamically typed)

concepts.intro: Operators combine values and variables into expressions that produce a result, covering arithmetic, comparison, and logic.
b: Arithmetic operators: + (add), - (subtract), * (multiply), / (divide), % (modulo/remainder)
Comparison operators: == (equal), != (not equal), <, >, <=, >= — these produce a boolean result
Logical operators: AND, OR, NOT combine boolean expressions (e.g., age >= 13 AND age <= 19)
Order of operations (PEMDAS-like precedence) applies: multiplication/division before addition/subtraction
The assignment operator (=) stores a value into a variable; it is different from the equality operator (==)

concepts.intro: Programs typically follow a pattern of receiving input, processing it, and producing output, structured as a sequence of statements executed in order.
b: Output statements (like print) display information to the user
Input statements collect data from the user, often read in as a string that may need converting to a number
A statement is a single instruction; a program is a sequence of statements executed top to bottom by default
Comments (e.g., starting with # or //) are ignored by the computer but help humans understand code
Syntax errors occur when code doesn't follow a language's grammar rules and won't run at all

concepts.intro: Errors (bugs) are inevitable in programming; recognizing the type of error is the first step to fixing it.
b: Syntax errors: code violates the language's grammar rules (e.g., missing a colon or parenthesis)
Runtime errors: code is valid but fails while running (e.g., dividing by zero, opening a missing file)
Logic errors: code runs without crashing but produces the wrong result due to flawed reasoning
Debugging strategies include reading error messages carefully, using print statements to trace values, and testing small pieces separately
A debugger is a tool that lets you pause execution and inspect variable values step by step

concepts.intro: Good programming style makes code easier to read, test, and maintain, both for yourself and others.
b: Use meaningful variable and function names instead of single letters like x or temp
Keep consistent indentation to show code structure (especially important in Python)
Break repeated logic into functions rather than copy-pasting the same code multiple times
Test code with a range of inputs, including edge cases like zero, negative numbers, or empty strings
Version control (like Git) tracks changes to code over time and allows collaboration

concepts.intro: Programming languages provide different tools and styles for expressing solutions, but most fundamentals transfer between them.
b: Popular beginner languages include Python, JavaScript, and Java, each with different syntax but similar core concepts
A compiler translates entire source code into machine code before running; an interpreter executes code line by line
High-level languages (like Python) are closer to human language; low-level languages (like assembly) are closer to hardware
Procedural programming organizes code as a sequence of steps/functions; object-oriented programming organizes code around objects with data and behavior
Libraries and frameworks provide pre-written code so programmers don't have to solve common problems from scratch

keyFacts: The modulo operator (%) returns the remainder of division, e.g., 7 % 2 = 1
In most languages, = assigns a value while == checks for equality
Python uses indentation to define code blocks; languages like Java use curly braces {}
A compiler translates code before execution; an interpreter translates and runs it line-by-line
traps: = is assignment (stores a value), not ==, which is comparison (checks equality)
A syntax error prevents code from running at all; a logic error lets code run but produces a wrong answer, not a crash
Concatenating strings with + joins text together, not adds numbers — '2' + '2' gives '22' in many languages, not 4
Compiled and interpreted are about when/how code is translated, not about which language is 'better' — both approaches are valid

quiz.q: What is the base of the binary number system?
quiz.e: Binary is base-2, using only digits 0 and 1.

quiz.q: How many bits are in one byte?
quiz.e: A byte is defined as a group of 8 bits.

quiz.q: What is the decimal value of binary 1011?
What is the decimal value of binary 1000?
quiz.e: 1000 has a 1 in the 8's place, so it equals 8.

quiz.q: Which component is volatile, meaning it loses its contents when power is off?
quiz.e: RAM is volatile memory used for temporary working data.

quiz.q: What does CPU stand for?
quiz.e: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit, the 'brain' of the computer.

quiz.q: What number system uses digits 0-9 and letters A-F?
quiz.e: Hexadecimal (base-16) uses 0-9 and A-F to represent values 0-15.

quiz.q: How many bits does one hexadecimal digit represent?
quiz.e: Each hex digit maps to exactly 4 bits (a nibble).

quiz.q: What is the primary purpose of an operating system?
o: To manage hardware resources and run other software
quiz.e: The OS manages memory, CPU scheduling, and hardware so other programs can run.

quiz.q: Which encoding standard supports characters from nearly every language, including emoji?
quiz.e: Unicode (commonly encoded as UTF-8) extends ASCII to support global characters.

quiz.q: What does the fetch-decode-execute cycle describe?
o: How data is saved to disk
quiz.e: This cycle describes the basic steps a CPU repeats to run a program.

quiz.q: Which of these is non-volatile storage?
quiz.e: SSDs retain data even without power, unlike RAM.

quiz.q: Convert decimal 6 to binary.
quiz.e: 6 = 4+2, so binary is 110.

quiz.q: Convert decimal 13 to binary.
quiz.e: 13 = 8+4+1, so binary is 1101.

quiz.q: What is a bit?
quiz.e: A bit is the smallest unit of data, either 0 or 1.

quiz.q: Approximately how many bytes are in a megabyte?
quiz.e: A megabyte is approximately one million bytes.

quiz.q: Which device would be classified as an input device?
quiz.e: A keyboard sends data into the computer, making it an input device.

quiz.q: What is the role of a GPU?
o: Handling parallel computations, especially graphics and AI
quiz.e: GPUs are optimized for parallel processing tasks like rendering graphics.

quiz.q: Why do computers use binary instead of decimal internally?
o: Binary is easier for humans to read
Transistors are simplest to build as two-state (on/off) switches
Binary uses less power than decimal
quiz.e: Two-state electrical switches map naturally onto binary's two digits.

quiz.q: What is the hexadecimal representation of decimal 255?
quiz.e: 255 in binary is 11111111, which splits into two nibbles of 1111 (F) each: FF.

quiz.q: What does ASCII primarily encode?
quiz.e: ASCII assigns numeric codes to letters, digits, and symbols.

quiz.q: What is clock speed typically measured in?
quiz.e: Clock speed, measuring CPU cycles per second, is measured in Hertz (e.g., GHz).

quiz.q: Which best distinguishes system software from application software?
o: System software supports the computer itself; application software helps users do tasks
quiz.e: The OS is system software; a browser or game is application software.

quiz.q: What happens to data stored only in RAM when the computer loses power?
o: It is automatically saved to the cloud
quiz.e: RAM is volatile, so unsaved data in RAM disappears when power is cut.

quiz.q: What is a 'driver' in the context of an operating system?
o: A person who codes the OS
A program that lets the OS communicate with specific hardware
quiz.e: Drivers translate between the OS and hardware devices like printers or graphics cards.

quiz.q: Which is an example of an operating system?
quiz.e: Linux is an operating system; the others are application software.

quiz.q: How is color often represented in web design?
quiz.e: Web colors are commonly written as 6-digit hex codes representing red, green, and blue values.

quiz.q: What does it mean for storage to be 'non-volatile'?
o: It retains data even when power is removed
quiz.e: Non-volatile storage like an SSD keeps data without continuous power.

quiz.q: What is a nibble?
quiz.e: A nibble is half a byte, or 4 bits, matching one hex digit.

quiz.q: Which best describes 'Moore's Law'?
o: An observation that transistor density roughly doubles every two years
quiz.e: Moore's Law is an observed trend in transistor miniaturization and growth, not a physical law.

quiz.q: What number system do humans typically use in daily life?
quiz.e: Humans generally count using base-10 (decimal), likely due to having ten fingers.

quiz.q: Which best describes how images are digitally stored?
o: As a grid of pixels, each with color values
quiz.e: Digital images are grids of pixels, each pixel storing color as binary data (e.g., RGB values).

quiz.q: What is the motherboard's function?
o: Physically connects and enables communication between components
quiz.e: The motherboard is the main circuit board linking CPU, RAM, storage, and other parts.

quiz.q: Convert binary 1111 to decimal.
What best explains why SSDs are generally preferred over traditional hard drives (HDDs)?
o: SSDs have no moving parts and are faster
quiz.e: SSDs use flash memory with no moving parts, making them faster and more durable than spinning HDDs.

quiz.q: What is the largest value a single byte (8 bits) can represent in unsigned binary?
quiz.e: 8 bits can represent 2^8 = 256 values, from 0 to 255.

quiz.q: Which pair correctly matches a unit with what it measures?
quiz.e: Hertz measures frequency/clock speed; bytes measure storage size.

quiz.q: What is sampling, in the context of digital audio?
o: Measuring a sound wave's amplitude at regular intervals to store as numbers
quiz.e: Digital audio is created by sampling the analog wave repeatedly and storing each measurement as a binary number.

quiz.q: Why might a text file be smaller than an image file of similar content length?
o: Text always compresses better than images by law
Images generally require far more data per unit of content (many pixels vs. characters)
Image files use binary, but text files do not
quiz.e: Images typically require storing information for many pixels, resulting in much larger raw data compared to compact character-based text.

quiz.q: What best describes the relationship between hardware and software?
o: Hardware is the physical machine; software is the instructions that tell hardware what to do
Software replaces the need for hardware
Hardware only exists in the cloud
quiz.e: Hardware is physical components; software consists of programs/instructions that control hardware behavior.

quiz.q: What is a variable in programming?
o: A fixed value that never changes
A named storage location that holds a value which can change
quiz.e: Variables store data that can be updated as the program runs.

quiz.q: Which data type would best store the value 3.14?
quiz.e: 3.14 has a decimal point, so it is a float (floating-point number).

quiz.q: What does the modulo operator (%) return?
quiz.e: Modulo returns the remainder of dividing one number by another.

quiz.q: What is the result of 7 % 2?
quiz.e: 7 divided by 2 is 3 remainder 1, so 7 % 2 = 1.

quiz.q: What does the == operator do?
o: Assigns a value to a variable
Checks if two values are equal
quiz.e: == is the equality comparison operator, returning true or false.

quiz.q: What kind of error occurs when code violates the grammar rules of a language?
quiz.e: Syntax errors happen when code doesn't follow the language's required structure.

quiz.q: What kind of error lets a program run but produces an incorrect result?
quiz.e: A logic error means the code runs, but the reasoning/algorithm is flawed.

quiz.q: What kind of error happens while a program is running, such as dividing by zero?
quiz.e: Runtime errors occur during execution, even if the syntax is valid.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a comment in code?
o: To be executed as an instruction
To explain code to human readers; it is ignored by the computer
quiz.e: Comments are notes for humans and are not executed by the program.

quiz.q: Which best describes a compiler?
o: A tool that translates the entire program into machine code before it runs
A tool that only checks spelling
A tool that deletes bugs automatically
quiz.e: Compilers translate the whole source code into machine code ahead of execution.

quiz.q: Which best describes an interpreter?
o: It compiles code once and never again
It executes code line-by-line, translating as it goes
It only works with binary files
quiz.e: Interpreters read and execute code one line/statement at a time.

quiz.q: In most languages, what is the difference between = and ==?
o: = assigns a value; == compares for equality
== assigns a value; = compares for equality
quiz.e: = stores a value into a variable, while == checks whether two values are equal.

quiz.q: What will '2' + '2' likely produce in many programming languages, where both values are strings?
quiz.e: Adding two strings typically concatenates them rather than performing math.

quiz.q: Which is an example of a boolean value?
quiz.e: Boolean values are only True or False.

quiz.q: What does an input statement typically do?
quiz.e: Input statements gather data (often as text) from the user during execution.

quiz.q: Why might input read from a user need to be converted before doing math with it?
o: Input is always already a number
Input is often read as a string/text, even if it looks like a number
Math cannot be performed in programs
quiz.e: Many languages read user input as text (a string), which must be converted to a numeric type for arithmetic.

quiz.q: What is the primary purpose of using functions instead of repeating code?
o: To avoid duplicating logic and make code reusable/organized
To increase the number of syntax errors
quiz.e: Functions let you reuse the same logic without copy-pasting it repeatedly.

quiz.q: What does 'static typing' mean?
o: Variable types are declared and fixed, checked before running
quiz.e: Statically typed languages require explicit types that are checked before the program runs.

quiz.q: What does 'dynamic typing' mean, as used in Python?
o: Variable types are determined automatically at runtime and can change
The language has no data types
quiz.e: Dynamically typed languages infer types automatically, and a variable's type can change.

quiz.q: What is version control (e.g., Git) primarily used for?
o: Tracking changes to code over time and enabling collaboration
quiz.e: Version control tracks historical changes and helps multiple people collaborate on code.

quiz.q: What does a debugger allow a programmer to do?
o: Pause execution and inspect variable values step by step
quiz.e: A debugger lets you step through code and examine program state to find bugs.

quiz.q: Which is considered a 'high-level' programming language?
quiz.e: Python is high-level, meaning its syntax is closer to human language than to hardware instructions.

quiz.q: What is an 'edge case' in testing?
o: An unusual or extreme input, like zero or an empty string, that might break code
quiz.e: Edge cases test boundary or unusual conditions that often reveal bugs.

quiz.q: What does the order of operations (operator precedence) determine?
o: The order in which parts of an expression are evaluated
quiz.e: Precedence rules dictate, e.g., that multiplication happens before addition unless parentheses override it.

quiz.q: Which logical operator returns true only if both conditions are true?
quiz.e: AND requires both operands to be true for the result to be true.

quiz.q: What does the NOT operator do to a boolean value?
o: Flips true to false and false to true
quiz.e: NOT inverts a boolean's value.

quiz.q: What is object-oriented programming primarily organized around?
o: A strict sequence of unrelated steps
Objects that bundle data and behavior together
quiz.e: OOP structures code as objects that combine data (attributes) and behavior (methods).

quiz.q: What is procedural programming primarily organized around?
o: Sequences of steps/functions performed in order
quiz.e: Procedural programming follows a step-by-step, function-based approach to solving problems.

quiz.q: Why use meaningful variable names like 'totalScore' instead of 'x'?
o: It makes the program run faster
It makes code more readable and easier to maintain
It is required by all compilers
quiz.e: Descriptive names improve readability without affecting program speed or correctness.

quiz.q: What is a library or framework in programming?
o: A physical building for storing computers
Pre-written code that provides reusable functionality
quiz.e: Libraries and frameworks give programmers reusable, pre-built code for common tasks.

quiz.q: What best describes 'concatenation' with strings?
o: Joining two or more strings together
quiz.e: Concatenation combines strings end-to-end, often using the + operator.

quiz.q: Which best explains why indentation matters in Python specifically?
o: It is purely stylistic and has no effect on the program
Python uses indentation to define code blocks/structure
quiz.e: Unlike many languages that use braces, Python relies on indentation to define blocks of code.

quiz.q: What happens if you try to divide a number by zero at runtime in many languages?
o: It typically causes a runtime error/exception
quiz.e: Division by zero is undefined and commonly raises a runtime error.

quiz.q: What is the result of the expression 2 + 3 * 4, following standard operator precedence?
quiz.e: Multiplication happens first (3*4=12), then addition: 2+12=14.

quiz.q: Which statement about testing with a range of inputs is most accurate?
o: Testing should include typical, boundary, and invalid inputs to catch bugs
Testing is unnecessary if code compiles
Only professional programmers need to test code
quiz.e: Thorough testing covers typical cases plus edge cases and invalid inputs.

quiz.q: What is a 'string' data type used for?
quiz.e: A string stores sequences of characters, i.e., text.

quiz.q: Why might a program with correct syntax still give the wrong answer?
o: This is impossible if syntax is correct
It may contain a logic error in its reasoning or algorithm
quiz.e: Syntax correctness only means the code will run — it doesn't guarantee the logic behind it is right.

quiz.q: What does 'readable code' primarily help with?
o: Helping humans understand, maintain, and debug the code later
Avoiding the need for an operating system
quiz.e: Readable code is easier for the original author or others to understand and maintain over time.

quiz.q: Which is an example of an arithmetic operator?
quiz.e: * (multiplication) is an arithmetic operator; the others are logical/comparison operators.

quiz.q: What does it mean for a program to execute 'top to bottom' by default?
o: Statements run in the order they are written unless control flow changes that
The last line always runs first
Only the first line ever executes
quiz.e: Without loops, conditionals, or function calls redirecting flow, a program executes statements sequentially from top to bottom.
